.  The petitioners have filed the present contempt petition under Section 12 of the Contempt of Court Act read with Article 215 of the Constitution of India alleging non-compliance of the order dated 24.01.2024 passed by this Court in WP(C) No. 3047/2018, wherein this Court has passed the following order:-
"6.

It is apparent that the land of the petitioner was acquired in the year 2018;
compensation was assessed and the cheque was prepared but the same could not be handed over to the petitioner on account of an objection of the intervener.

From the perusal of the documents, it appears that the objection raised by the intervener has not been decided by the Land Acquisition Officer, therefore, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, the present petition is disposed of with a direction to the Land Acquisition Officer to decide the objection raised by the intervener and thereafter pass an appropriate order.

The petitioner as well as the intervener would be at liberty to produce relevant documents showing their right over the suit Smt. Harinder Kaur Chawla vs Mr. Nand Kumar Choubey on 7 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171418331/
1 property.

entities.text: Smt. Harinder Kaur Chawla vs Mr. Nand Kumar Choubey on 7 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If it is found that the petitioner is the owner and title holder of the land acquired, then the amount of compensation shall be paid to the petitioner immediately thereafter."

2. Learned counsel for the respondent would submit that the respondents have intended to comply with the order passed by this Court, but since the dispute is pending between Harinder Kaur Chawla and Reshma Priti, as such, he cannot adjudicate the issue.
This fact has been observed in the order dated 20.06.2024 passed by the Sub-Divisional Officer respondent No. 1 who is Land Acquisition Officer also and accordingly, he has closed the proceedings.
This finding cannot be said to be illegal or non- compliance of the order passed by this Court.

3. Once the dispute between the parties is pending before the duly constituted authority under the law, therefore, the learned SDO has rightly not decided the issue, as such no case for initiating contempt proceeding is made out.

However, the appellate authority i.e. Commissioner where the proceeding is pending is expected to decide the case expeditiously within 4 months from the date of receipt of copy of order, if it has not been decided till today.
4. With the aforesaid observation and direction, the contempt petition is disposed of.

Sd/-
(Narendra Kumar Vyas) Judge Manish Smt. Harinder Kaur Chawla vs Mr. Nand Kumar Choubey on 7 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171418331/
